_comment: Tells somebody when ../detectors/waitlist-submit-failed.json raises an
issue. Its own workflow on purpose: the hand-made monitor this replaces
was connected in the UI to 'Website error (production)', which made
that workflow listen to a detector website-errors.json does not
describe, and apply.sh has refused to update it ever since (ONL-119).
One file, one detector, keeps the refusal meaningful.
detectorName is required: it is how this file finds a detector apply.sh
created itself, and the name is the only handle that survives the
detector being recreated.
regression_event is the trigger that matters, and first_seen_event
alone was SEEN NOT TO FIRE. A metric monitor raises ONE issue and
reopens it on every later breach. ONLOOKER-MARKETING-5 was first seen
2026-09-26, so the forced failure on 2026-10-26 at 23:46Z added an
occurrence to it at 23:51:49Z. The issue was not new, so the workflow
never triggered (lastTriggered null, empty group history) and nobody
was emailed. first_seen_event stays only for the case where the
detector is recreated and raises a fresh issue.
The email goes to the team by id, unlike every other file here, and
email/issue_owners was SEEN NOT TO DELIVER. With regression_event the
workflow fired at 2026-10-27T01:42:18Z, and no email ever arrived for
ONLOOKER-MARKETING-5, on that fire or on its creation 2026-09-26. Error
issues in the same project (-4, -6, -7) and the cron alert all emailed
through issue_owners. The difference is the detector's owner: a metric
issue is owned by team:onlooker, so the AllMembers fallthrough never
applies. Naming the team says who is told instead of leaving it to
ownership rules, and the id is the same team the detector names as its
owner. It reaches only the team's members, so whoever should be paged
must be on team onlooker.
Both changes together were SEEN TO DELIVER: a failure forced at
2026-10-27T02:42:23Z reopened ONLOOKER-MARKETING-5, the workflow fired
at 02:48:26Z, and the email reached a team member.
